narrative.overview: Aurora feels like dependable field equipment activated under a moving night sky. The field-manual foundation remains direct, legible, and evidence-led; controlled aurora light supplies motion, depth, and a memorable sense of readiness. Aurora Survival remains the flagship within the Aurora product family, with a quiet family label and compact Aurora Digest footer mention. The system is a mature SaaS presentation grounded in an outdoor product. It uses real product evidence, strong section pacing, and restrained atmospheric effects without generic AI particles, fake dashboards, decorative chat bubbles, or invented claims.
keyCharacteristics: A cinematic full-width first viewport with slow teal, blue, and violet light.
Full-width chapters with centered content measures and no negative section overlap.
Physical-device proof as the primary product material.
A crisp pixel wildlife detection graphic within the species scanner field.
Warm paper reading sections separated by decisive dark product moments.
Square controls, thin rules, compact measurement labels, and generous space.
One coordinated motion language that becomes completely static when requested.
Quiet product-family labeling that keeps Aurora Survival visually primary.

rules.name: The Aurora Field Rule
rules.body: Saturated teal, blue, and violet may move across dark atmospheric surfaces. Reading surfaces remain restrained, and saturated color never replaces product evidence.

rules.name: The Plain Language Rule
rules.body: Let scale and weight supply authority; copy stays concrete and never performs futurism.

rules.name: The Physical Evidence Rule
rules.body: Depth supports real product evidence; it never turns ordinary content into floating UI chrome.

dos: Do use real app captures whenever describing product behavior.
Do keep claims traceable to product documentation or repository evidence.
Do use light, motion, spacing, and scale to lead attention.
Do preserve keyboard focus, mobile readability, no-JavaScript content, and reduced motion.
Do keep the BioCLIP, founder GitHub, and Aurora Digest repository links descriptive and safe.
donts: Don't add particles, glowing orbs, fake dashboards, testimonials, customer logos, or decorative chat bubbles.
Don't turn sections into interchangeable rounded cards or oversized pills.
Don't introduce web fonts, trackers, or third-party runtime assets.
Don't publish the founder's name in page copy; use contact and profile links.
Don't imply the App Store release is currently available.
